newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips end strong; bond yield at 6-1/2 month low.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips end strong; bond yield at 6-1/2 month low.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed with strong gains Tuesday as fresh economic reports calmed inflation jitters and sent long-term interest rates plunging to the lowest levels in more than 6-1/2 months.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended 34.29 points higher at 6,007.02. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,292 to 1,142 on active volume of 441 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Treasury's 30-year bond soared nearly 2 points and its yield sank to 6.68 percent -- its lowest level since April 4 -- and compared with 6.84 percent on Monday.
"The bond market liked the economic data and pulled stocks along with it to a point," said Bob Stovall, president of Stovall/21st Advisers.

Financial markets were buoyed by a smaller-than-expected rise in the government's index of workers' compensation for the third quarter, which was up 0.6 percent after a 0.8 percent gain in the previous three months.
The overall increase in employee compensation costs in the third quarter -- the smallest in a year -- was below the 0.8 percent rise expected by Wall Street economists.

Also boosting sentiment was the consumer confidence index, which fell to 106.2 in October from a revised 111.8 in September. The figure was expected at 110.6, according to a Reuter survey of economists.

"People are thinking no Fed tightening for the rest of the year and after the first of (next) year, there might be thinking of a Fed loosening," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal & Co.
Interest-rate sensitive shares bounded higher, with Wells Fargo up 3-5/8 to 264-1/8, Freddie Mac up 2-1/8 to 99-3/8, while Citicorp jumped 2-3/8 to 97-3/8 and Fannie Mae added 7/8 to 37-7/8.
The rush of economic reports resumes on Wednesday with the release of third-quarter gross domestic product and Friday's unemployment data for October.
GDP is seen rising at a 1.8 percent annual rate, cooling down from the 4.7 percent second-quarter growth rate. The jobless rate is expected to hold steady at 5.2 percent.
But traders were cautious on the approach of next week's elections.
"There's an overhanging fear of a one-party leadership as of next Tuesday and that will weigh on stocks no matter what the day-to-day news is," said Stovall.

The technology-studded Nasdaq Composite slumped 12.84 points to 1,203.05 after Salomon Brothers said there has been a softening in retail computer sales over the last few weeks, which pressured the stocks of computer makers and retailers.
CompUSA shed 5-7/8 to 51-1/2, Tandy lost 1 to 39, Compaq was off 3-1/8 to 67-1/2, International Business Machines fell 1-5/8 to 125-1/2 and Dell shed 4-7/8 to 76-1/8.
America Online rose 1-1/8 to 25-3/4 after introducing a new corporate structure and a set of pricing plans to make it more competitive.
Donna Karan lost 3-1/2 to 15-1/4. The designer forecast break-even fourth-quarter results due to weakness at its beauty division.
DSP Communications tumbled 17-1/8 to 35-1/4 after announcing a $400 million merger with Proxim Inc., whose stock rose 2-51/64 to 21-1/2.
Premonos Technology slumped 9 to 7-5/8 on a quarterly loss and the resignation of a top executive.
SyStemix lost 1-3/4 to 14-1/4 after independent directors rejected an unsolicited offer from Sandoz Ltd. of $17 a share.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.24 points to 701.50. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.66 to 565.89.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.15 to 373.13. The average share was up 22 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,813.121 up 20.531 or 0.30 percent.
